These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0001] Round money only via round_money: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 1 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with code and repr payload: Reject invalid input by raising `BillingError(code, detail)` from `ledgerly.errors`, using codes like `invalid_state`, `invalid_quantity`, `negative_amount` and `repr(...)` of the offending value as detail.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)

texts.at-0001: Round money only via round_money Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
texts.at-0002: Normalize money via to_money and round_money Always pass monetary values through `to_money` and round results with `round_money` from `ledgerly.money`; compare against `ZERO` rather than a literal Decimal.
texts.at-0003: Raise BillingError with code and repr payload Reject invalid input by raising `BillingError(code, detail)` from `ledgerly.errors`, using codes like `invalid_state`, `invalid_quantity`, `negative_amount` and `repr(...)` of the offending value as detail.
texts.at-0004: Exclude bool when validating integers When validating an integer argument, reject `bool` explicitly with `isinstance(x, bool)` since `True`/`False` are ints in Python.
